key_insight: Model Carving jointly learns Transformer weights and topology, yielding smaller, heterogeneous models that outperform fixed-architecture baselines.
engineering_relevance: Removing sublayers during training reduces inference cost, with reported savings of up to 34% in FLOPs per token and up to 1.6× faster decoding without quality loss.
method: Attach learnable scalar gates to attention and MLP sublayers.
Let the training loss drive sublayer removal while optimizing model weights.
Retain the resulting smaller, heterogeneous network for inference.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on standard Transformers spanning 140M–2.7B parameters and looped Transformers spanning 140M–1.3B, carved models achieved lower validation loss than dense baselines trained with up to 1.7× more compute and outperformed size-matched pruned or distilled models.
watch_item: Real-world speedups should be verified on target hardware, since FLOP reductions do not guarantee proportional latency improvements.
paper_title: Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology
